text.p: Swiss shares extended earlier losses after Wall Street slipped following the release of the Philadelphia Fed index, dealers said.
They said stocks had already failed to move higher earlier despite gains on Wall Street on Wednesday, adding that the market still appeared to be in a period of consolidation.
The Swiss Market Index (SMI) of leading shares ended down 21.8 points, or 0.56 percent, at 3,861.5 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) was down 12.26 points, or 0.49 percent, at 2,469.43.
Interest was focused on special situations. Shares in technology group SEZ Holding continued their spectacular upward move on high volumes in their second day of trading.
The stock jumped nearly seven percent to 1,660 francs. High technology group Micronas added 40 francs to 1,090.
Among financials, SBC and insurers Zurich and Baloise rose. SBC added one franc to 254. Zurich rose two francs to 371 on a recommendation and new options. Baloise was up 45 francs.

UBS first soared early on speculative buying ahead of next Tuesday's news conference but then gave up the gains to end nine francs lower at 1,265. CS Holding edged down 1.50 francs to 135.00. Winterthur was down eight to 785 on profit taking.
Roche certificates fell below the 10,000 franc level, giving up 70 francs to end at 9,950. Ciba and Sandoz were weaker.
Alusuisse was up eight to 1,003. Buy recommendations and purchases by both domestic and foreign investors helped the stock, one dealer said.
